- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 10-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model shows persistent overconfidence; apply mean-reversion correction toward 10-day moving average.
- Forecast errors cluster in the last 5–7 days of 30-day horizon; adjust downward for final 5 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- When sentiment history shows no recent positive signals, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate.
